name: Regrow severed axons across the injury
description: Have descending axons — corticospinal and other motor tracts — regrow through or around the lesion and reach the grey matter below it.

grade.note: In rodents, combining a growth-permissive substrate, chemoattraction and neuron-intrinsic activation regrew propriospinal axons across a complete transection (Anderson 2018); neural stem cell grafts supported long-distance axon growth after severe injury (Lu 2012). Both are rodent. Human neural stem cell grafts have been placed in the primate cord with graft-derived axon extension (Rosenzweig 2018), which is the strongest large-animal evidence but still structure rather than function.
grade.drift: 'Paralysis reversed in mice' — regrowth across a lesion has been achieved; what those axons then do is a separate and mostly unanswered question.

wouldMove: Regrowth across a complete lesion in a non-human primate with a measured motor benefit, from a group unaffiliated with the original.
